metadata.description: Personal, portable toolkit of reusable Claude systems: skills, rules, hooks, and templates shared across every project and device.

plugins.name: project-init
plugins.description: Two skills: project-init walks you through setting up a new project (scaffolding, hooks, memory system, knowledge layer, CLAUDE.md) one skippable gate at a time; project-sync audits an existing project against the toolkit and closes the gaps you approve.

plugins.name: sf-architect-solutioning
plugins.description: Salesforce solution architect skill: pushes back on vague requirements, verifies platform facts against official Salesforce docs (live fetch, never memory), designs declarative-first to Well-Architected standards, and produces an approved solution plan before any build.

plugins.name: second-brain
plugins.description: Portable second-brain memory and knowledge architecture (MCP): a shared Cloudflare Worker MCP server backed by a per-project Neon Postgres/pgvector database and GitHub OAuth, holding a typed-node knowledge graph curated by two background agents, with hybrid keyword+vector recall, an auto-injected session digest and per-prompt recall injection, drift-pinned knowledge nodes, work-item tracking that reads status from the project's work-items folder tree rather than storing it (so 'is this done already?' cannot go stale) while memory holds the want and the links, per-turn capture, optional server-side auto-curation scoped to a finished chat session (a SessionEnd hook curates the conversation as one arc so cloud sessions curate automatically, with a cron backstop for sessions that die before ending), and a self-verifying harness. Reachable from the terminal and cloud sessions. Bundles a structural layer for mechanical impact analysis: a compiled Salesforce metadata dependency graph for Salesforce projects, and graphify (a local tree-sitter code graph covering Swift, web, and generic repos) for every other project type. Includes a one-time knowledge-base backfill plus ongoing-freshness hooks for onboarding onto existing codebases (any project type). An install skill sets it up per project from bundled reference implementations (a project-type question picks the profile); a second skill, remember, is a wrap-up command that dispatches the curators, both of them, so the often-forgotten knowledge-curator actually runs, to save a finished work item into the project's second brain.

plugins.name: git-workflows
plugins.description: Two parallel-session-safe git sync skills. pull-latest brings a checkout up to date with its remote without rewriting or discarding history (fetch, fast-forward, or merge pull; never rebase, reset, or push). reset-to-remote hard-resets a repo to exactly mirror its remote, the safe alternative to deleting and re-cloning. Both assume other agent sessions may share the repo and stop rather than clobber in-flight work.

plugins.name: session-autoname
plugins.description: Keeps a background Claude Code agent session named after the single overarching PROJECT it is working toward, not the step it happens to be on. A Stop hook runs at the end of every turn and asks Haiku for a short project-level label, judged from the arc of the owner's own requests (never the assistant's replies, which narrate the current step) and anchored by feeding the current name back in so it is returned unchanged unless the project genuinely changed. Keeps the job list accurate as a long session drifts off the task it started on, without the name churning every few minutes. Background sessions only, never blocks a turn, and fails silently if Claude Code's internal state format changes.
